reason: A earns my trust by admitting the A1C numbers come from only fourteen people and that medication changes weren't tracked, and it lets me try a week or call first without pressure. B bolds the A1C figure, drops the medication caveat, leans on "real numbers from real customers", and adds details that aren't in the facts (a 10-meal trial, an address checker), which reads like the pitches I've fallen for before.
